title: They Always Ask Us...
text:
They always ask us

to understand the point of view

of others

no matter whether it is

outdated

foolish

disgusting.

One is asked

to understand

kindly

all the errors of others

their wasted lives

especially if they are

advanced in age.

But their age is the only thing

we notice.

They have aged

badly

because they have

lived

without focus,

they have refused

to see.

Is it not their fault?

whose fault?

mine?

I am asked to hide

my opinion

before them

for fear of their

fear.

Age is not a crime

but the shame

of a life

deliberately

wasted

among so many

lives

deliberately

wasted

is.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the accusatory line breaks and the distinction between age itself and deliberate waste.

title: Letter from Far Away
text:
She wrote me a letter from a small

room near the Seine.

she said she was going to take

dance classes. She got up, she said,

at exactly 5 in the morning

and typed poems

or painted

and when she felt like crying

she had a special bench

beside the river.


Her book of Cantos

would go out

in the Fall.


I did not know what to tell her

but

I told her

I would have any bad teeth pulled

and to be careful of the

French lover.


I put her photo beside the radio

near the fan

and it moved

like something

alive.


I sat and watched it

until I had smoked

5 or 6

remaining cigarettes.

Then I got up

and went to bed.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the distant letter, practical reply, moving photo, and lonely smoking.

title: When God Created Love He Didn't Help Much...
text:
when God created love he didn't help much

when God created dogs he didn't help dogs

when God created plants he wasn't very original

when God created hate we had something useful


when God created me, well, he created me


when God created the monkey he was asleep

when he created the giraffe he was drunk

when he created drugs he was high

and when he created suicide he was depressed


when he created you sleeping in bed

he knew what he was doing

he was drunk and high

and created the mountains and the sea and fire at the same time


he made some mistakes

but when he created you sleeping in bed

he spilled himself over his Blessed Universe
editorial_note: The translation keeps the comic irreverence toward creation and the sudden praise of the beloved asleep.

title: She Writes...
text:
She writes

continually

like a long sprayer

spraying

the air,

and argues

continually;

there is nothing

I can say

that is not really

something else,

then,

I stop talking;

and finally

she argues with herself

outside the door

saying

something like

I am not trying to

impress myself

through you.


but I know

she will be

back, they always

come back.


and

at 5 p.m.

she was knocking at the door.

I let her in


I won't stay long, she said,

if you don't want me to.

it's all right, I said,

I'm going to take a

bath.


she went to the kitchen and

started on the

dishes.


like being married,

you accept

everything

as if it had

been that way.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the domestic loop of argument, return, dishes, and resignation.

title: The Raw Material for Love
text:
Girl

with brown skin full of kindness

if for any reason you grab the knife

I want you to know

I do not blame you.

And when I drive

along the coast with those old ugly palms

and the living who never arrive

and the dead who do not leave

I want you to know

I do not blame you.

I will remember you

for those long hours of kisses

with our lips swollen with love

and how you offered me your pussy, your soul,

your inside and how I answered you

by offering you the little

that remained of me.

I want you to know

I will always remember the size of your room,

the shape of your body,

your records,

the walls,

the coffee cups,

your mornings, your noons

beside your bad

nights.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the intimate, coarse register of the source while preserving its repeated refusal to blame.
